production.format_and_medium.summary: If information constituting a non-exempt identifiable public record is held in an electronic format, the agency must make it available in an electronic format when requested by any person.

The agency must make the information available in any electronic format in which it holds the information, and must provide a copy in the requested format if that format is one the agency has used to create copies for its own use or for other agencies.

waiver.notes: The CPRA has no fee-waiver provision (no indigency, public-interest, or media waiver; no purpose statement — § 7921.300 forbids purpose-based access limits; no written denial or appeal of a fee decision). waiver.forfeiture.label: Late response forfeits the fee
waiver.forfeiture.notes: No rule that a late determination or late production forfeits the fee; the CPRA's remedy for delay is judicial (§ 7923.000 et seq., with attorney fees to a prevailing requester under § 7923.115). fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: Fees for copies of records are limited to fees covering the direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if one applies.

fee.electronic_media_charge.summary: The cost of duplicating an electronic record is limited to the direct cost of producing a copy of the record in an electronic format.
